description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — September 15, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: QwenLM/qwen-code is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: QwenLM/qwen-code leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: QwenLM/qwen-code — 4 commits today and 1 same-day mapped article, 34.7 below its current daily pace, with 4 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 131 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
anomalyco/opencode — No same-day commit after 30 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Before adopting Kilo’s new board default, separate a stored note from a task control
dailyInsight.insight: Kilo’s September 14 source change enables the shared agent board by default and lets an explicit opt-out win. Operators evaluating that change should check what their coordination logic treats as success: a stored post does not establish that another agent read it, acted, or stopped.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The board resolver enables the feature unless its configuration or specific environment flag explicitly disables it. The board’s documented contract separates message storage from task execution: posts do not wake or resume recipients, and HOLD/VETO notes do not pause or cancel work.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A team can appear to coordinate while waiting for a finished worker or assuming an advisory message halted a conflicting edit. The new default makes these semantics relevant to operators who did not previously opt into the board.

actions.audience: Operators testing Kilo’s default-on shared board source change
actions.label: Audit one stopped-recipient exchange
actions.instruction: In a disposable session on a build containing the default-on change, complete a child task and post a follow-up. Confirm the returned recipient state and that the task remains completed. Check the installed version and explicit opt-out settings before applying any default assumption to a working environment.

receipts.title: Enable the Kilo Swarm shared board by default
receipts.supports: The resolver defaults on, either explicit false wins, the umbrella flag no longer controls the feature, and the opt-out moves to Agent Behaviour.

receipts.title: Kilo Swarm’s documented communication boundaries
receipts.supports: The settings documentation states that posts are stored messages, notices are best-effort, recipients are not a privacy boundary, and HOLD/VETO are advisory rather than execution controls.

confidence.basis: The changed default resolver, its explicit-disable tests, current tool implementation and public settings documentation agree on the narrow source behavior. Live agent compliance was not tested.

dailyInsight.limitation: This is a source-level change. At the September 15 reporting check, the latest published v7.6.2 still documented opt-in behavior. The source does not establish rollout, receipt by a model, or whether a model obeys the coordination instructions.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise the call if a subsequent implementation makes posting a task-control operation with verified delivery or acknowledgment, or if the default-on change is reverted before release.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a release carrying the September 14 default and tests showing how models handle stopped-recipient warnings and advisory hold messages.
